At n=7 and n=8, checked all 595 and 1540 endpoint pairs, respectively, finding thresholds 16 and 43 and 21 and 420 distinct maxima, with 10 and 1 witness pairs per maximum.
correctness.rationale: A nonresolving set is contained in a distance bisector, so the threshold is the largest bisector size plus one. At n=7 intersections of size 0,1,2,3 give distances 1,3,2,0. In the distance-three case with endpoints abc and ade and remaining points f,g, the path through def and bcg proves the upper bound, and no common disjoint triple exists. Equal distances then mean equal counts in the exclusive parts. For exclusive size k=3,2,1, the sum of binom(k,j)^2 binom(7−2k,3−2j) is 9,13,15 respectively. The 15-sets depend only on the pair of switched points, recoverable by their multiplicities 5 rather than 7. For n≥8 all nonadjacent distinct pairs have distance two. With q=binom(n−3,3) and c_r=binom(n−6+r,3), the number of distinguishers for overlap r is 2(q−c_r) plus two if r>0 (adjacent endpoints are already counted). This is strictly minimized at r=2, since c2>c1 and c2−c0>1, already at n=8. Its value is 2+2 binom(n−4,2). For overlap two, distinguishers are the two endpoints and the triples avoiding their shared pair K and choosing exactly one switch point in T. Ground-point frequencies on K, the complement of K∪T, and T are 2, 2(n−5), and 1+binom(n−4,2) in strictly increasing order, even at n=8. Thus both K and T are uniquely recoverable and the labelled census follows.
residual_risks: The independent finite reproduction is limited to n=7,8. The proof, not the computations, validates the all-order result. Smaller inclusion-maximal nonresolving sets are outside the claim.
